column2: Having saluted the perfected one who moves through all worlds, the eternal treasury of Brahman, the priest, he began to ask him this.
[Saudasa said:] Blessed one, what in the three worlds is called the purifier, sinless one, by reciting which a mortal would always gain the highest merit?
[Bhishma said:] To him who bowed, the learned one, pure, saluting the cows, then spoke beneficial words, the Upanishad of cows.
Cows are fragrant like perfume and like guggulu; cows are the support of beings, cows are the great well-being.
Cows are the past and the future, cows are eternal nourishment, cows are the root of Lakshmi; what is given to cows is not lost; cows are constantly food and the highest offering of the gods.
Svaha and vashat are always established in cows; cows are the fruit of sacrifice, and sacrifices are established in cows.
Morning and evening constantly, at the time of the fire offering, greatly wise one, cows give to the sages what is to be offered, bull among men.
Whatever hard places and misdeeds have been done, those who give a cow cross over sin, lord.
One who has not placed the fire, one with a hundred cows, a non-sacrificer, one with a thousand cows, and the rich miser: these three do not deserve guest-honour.
Those who give a tawny cow with calf and bronze milk-pail, of good vows, wrapped in a garment, conquer both worlds.
Those who give to a chief brahmana a young bull, lord of cows, endowed with senses, leader of a herd with a hundred, many-horned and adorned,
to a Shrotriya, scorcher of foes, are born again and again with lordship.
One should not sleep without naming cows nor rise without remembering them; one should bow to cows morning and evening; then one would gain nourishment.
One should never be disgusted by cow urine and dung, nor eat their flesh; thus one gains the cow's blessing.
One should always name the cows and not slight them; seeing an inauspicious dream, a man should name the cow.
One should always bathe with cow dung, lie down on cow dung, and avoid phlegm, urine, excrement and blows.
One should eat on a wet hide facing the west, silent, with ghee on the ground; thus one gains the cow's blessing.
One should offer ghee in the fire, have a blessing spoken with ghee, give ghee, taste ghee; thus one gains the cow's blessing.
One who with the Gomati science consecrates a sesame cow and gives it made of juices and jewels does not grieve over what is done and undone.

May cows wait on me, gold-horned, releasing milk, fragrant, the Saurabheyis, as rivers to the sea.
mahabharata:13:77.23	May cows always see me; may I see cows; the cows are ours, we are theirs; where the cows are, there are we.
Thus night and day, in smooth and rough places and in great fears, a man reciting is freed from fear.
In this world, of all fees may we be the best, and not be stained by fault, scorcher of foes.
By that same thought one killed is always stained; and the gods and men make use of dung for purification.
So all beings, moving and unmoving, and the givers, giver of honour, would go to the world of cows.
At the end of austerity Brahma, the self-lord, gave them a boon: "So be it; and carry the worlds across."
Wishing success they arose, the mothers of past and future, at the end of austerity, great king, cows whose goal was the worlds.
Therefore cows are greatly fortunate and said to be the highest purifier; so for all beings cows stand on the head.
Giving a milch tawny cow with a calf of her own colour, of good vows, wrapped in a garment, he is honoured in Brahma's world.
Giving a milch Rohini cow with a calf of equal colour, of good vows, wrapped in a garment, he is honoured in the world of the sun.
Giving a milch black cow with a calf of her own colour, of good vows, wrapped in a garment, he is honoured in the world of fire.
Giving a milch smoke-coloured cow with a calf of the same colour, of good vows, wrapped in a garment, he is honoured in Yama's world.
Giving one the colour of water-foam, with calf and bronze milk-pail, wrapped in a garment, he gains Varuna's world.
Giving one the colour of wind-dust, with calf and bronze milk-pail, wrapped in a garment, he is honoured in the world of wind.
Giving one of golden colour with tawny eyes, with calf and bronze milk-pail, wrapped in a garment, he gains Kubera's world.
Giving one the colour of straw-smoke, with calf and bronze milk-pail, wrapped in a garment, he is honoured in the world of the ancestors.
Giving a stout cow with calf, dark-necked and adorned, he reaches the Vishvedeva place, unobstructed and best.
Giving a milch white cow with a calf of the same colour, of good vows, wrapped in a garment, he gains the world of the Vasus.
Giving one the colour of a pale blanket, with calf and bronze milk-pail, wrapped in a garment, he gains the world of the Sadhyas.
Giving a bull of Virata back, adorned with all jewels, he reaches the ageless worlds of the Maruts.
Giving a blue-limbed cow with calf, joined with all jewels, a man gains the worlds of gandharvas and apsarases.
Giving a dark-necked ox adorned with all jewels, he reaches the worlds of Prajapati, free of sorrow.
Devoted to giving cows, he goes, breaking through masses of clouds, in a sun-coloured celestial car shining in the sky, king.
A thousand fair-hipped, finely dressed best women delight that man devoted to the gift of cows, best of men.
With the sounds of lutes, vallakis and anklets and the laughter of deer-eyed women, the sleeper is awakened.
For as many years as the cow has hairs he is honoured, and fallen from heaven, he will be born in the world of men in the family of owners of cows.

Ghee is always in my heart, ghee is set in my navel, ghee in all my limbs, ghee is established in my mind.
mahabharata:13:79.3	Cows are always before me and cows behind me, cows on all sides of me, and I live in the midst of cows.
Sipping water so and muttering morning and evening, a man is always freed from the sin he does by day.
Where there are golden palaces and where the stream of wealth is, where gandharvas and apsarases are, there go the givers of thousands.
Where rivers flow with butter for mud, milk for water, and curds for weeds, there go the givers of thousands.
One who duly gives a hundred thousand cows, having gained supreme prosperity, is honoured in the world of cows.
After death he places ten on both sides, his mother's and father's ancestors, in worlds of good deeds, and purifies his family.
Giving a cow, and a sesame cow equal in measure to a cow, and the giver of drinking water meets no torment in Yama's world.
Giving a tawny cow with calf, many-horned, with a bronze milk-pail, and a garment as covering, a man fearless enters Yama's assembly, hard to enter.
One should constantly recite, "May the cows, of fine form, many forms and all forms, mothers, wait on me."
There is no gift more holy than this, no fruit more holy than this, nothing more distinguished in the worlds can exist.
With hide, hair, horns, tail, milk and fat they together carry the sacrifice; what is greater than that?
I bow with my head to that cow by whom this whole moving and unmoving world is pervaded, the mother of past and future.
This is one part of the assembly of qualities of cows, king, told to you by me; there is no higher gift than to cows, nor is there any other refuge.
[Bhishma said:] "This is supreme," thinking so, the great-souled lord of earth, self-controlled, gave to the twice-born very many cows according to the sage's excellent word, and gained worlds.
[Bhishma said:] Cows are of great worth and holy, and carry men across; they sustain these creatures with milk and offering.
Nothing is more holy than cows, best of the Bharatas; they are purifying and holy, unsurpassed in the three worlds.
Cows live above the gods; having given them, wise men go to heaven, lord of men.
Mandhatri, Yuvanashva's son, Yayati and Nahusha, constantly giving cows counted by hundreds of thousands, went to the supreme place hard to reach even for gods.
On this too I shall tell you an ancient event, sinless one.
Shuka, saluting Krishna Dvaipayana, the wise best of sages, having done the day's rite, pure and composed in mind, asked his father who had seen the high and low worlds:

What sacrifice is seen to be best of all sacrifices? By doing what do the wise gain supreme heaven?
mahabharata:13:80.9	By what purifier do the gods enjoy heaven, lord? What is the sacrificial nature of sacrifice, and where is sacrifice established?
Hearing these words, Vyasa, knower of supreme dharma, told his son everything in truth, bull of the Bharatas.
[Vyasa said:] Cows are the foundation of beings and their refuge; cows are holy and pure, a purifier and dharma itself.
We have heard that cows were formerly hornless; for horns they waited on the imperishable lord.
Then Brahma, seeing the cows seated, fasting, gave each cow the wish she desired.
Horns arose for them, for each as she wished in mind; of various colours, with horns, they shone, my son.
Given boons by Brahma, they became givers of offerings to gods and ancestors, lovely, holy, pure, fortunate, with divine form and marks; cows are great divine splendour; the gift of cows is praised.
Those good people who give them, free of envy, are called doers of good and givers of all gifts, and they gain the world of cows as merit, sinless one.
Where trees have honey for fruit, bearing divine flowers and fruits, and flowers are fragrant and divine, best of the twice-born,
the whole ground is made of jewels, with fine golden sand, everywhere pleasant to touch, mudless, dustless, and lovely.
With groves of red lotuses and jewelled stalks of gold, the lakes shine there like the young sun.
With costly jewel leaves and gold filaments, with lakes mixed with blue lotuses and many lotuses,
adorned with flowering oleander groves covered with thousand-whirled things, flowering Santanaka groves and trees,
with clear pearls and costly gems, the banks of rivers there are raised, with gold,
entered by wonderful best mountains made wholly of jewels and others of gold, bright as fire.
There are golden mountains, heaps of rocks of jewels, shining with lovely high peaks made wholly of jewels.
Trees there always have flowers and fruit, crowded with birds, with divine scents and juices, with flowers and fruits, bull of the Bharatas.
Doers of merit always delight there, Yudhishthira, rich in the objects of all desires, sorrowless and free of anger.
In wonderful and lovely celestial cars, Bharata, the glorious doers of merit rejoice, roaming.
Auspicious troops of apsarases play around them, king; by giving a cow he gains those worlds, Yudhishthira.

Those whose lord is Pushan, the mighty Maruta, and in lordship King Varuna, may those cow-bearers protect me.
mahabharata:13:80.31	Of fine form, many forms and all forms, mothers, children of Prajapati: thus, brahmana, one should mutter always, of controlled vow.
He who serves cows and follows them in every way: pleased, they give him boons even very hard to get.
One should not injure them even in mind, for they give happiness; one should always worship and honour them with salutations, self-controlled and glad, and so gain the cows' blessing.
By which purifier the gods enjoy the highest world, that purifier of purifiers, ghee, one should bear on the head.
One should offer ghee in the fire, have a blessing spoken with ghee, taste ghee, give ghee; thus one gains the cow's blessing.

One should drink warm urine for three days, warm milk for three days; having drunk the cows' warm milk, drink warm ghee for three days; having drunk warm ghee for three days, live on air for three days.
With barley taken from the cows' dung, living a month on a handful of barley-gruel, all sin equal to killing a brahmana is purified by this.
For the defeat of the Daityas this purification was made by the gods; they gained godhood and perfection and great strength.
Cows are holy and pure, a great supreme purifier; having given them to the twice-born, a man gains heaven.
Pure in the midst of cows, one should mutter the Gomati in mind; sipping pure water, one becomes pure and clean.
In the midst of fire, in the midst of cows and in the assembly of brahmanas, brahmanas who are bathed in learning and Vedic vows and do meritorious deeds
should teach pupils the Gomati, equal to a sacrifice; having fasted three nights and heard the Gomati, one gains a boon.
One desiring a son gains a son, and wealth too; a woman desiring a husband gains a husband; a man gains all desires; cows, pleased, give when served, without doubt.
Thus these greatly fortunate sacrificial cows are givers of all desires; know them as Rohinis; there is nothing higher than they.
Thus addressed by his great-souled father, the greatly radiant Shuka always worshipped cows; therefore you too worship them.
[Bhishma said:] On this too they recite this ancient Itihasa, the conversation of Shri and the cows, king, best of the Bharatas.
Shri, having made her body lovely, entered the midst of the cows; the cows were astonished, seeing the wealth of her beauty.
[The cows said:] "Who are you, goddess, and whence? Incomparable on earth in beauty, we are astonished, greatly fortunate one, at the wealth of your beauty.
We wish to know who you are and where you will go; tell us all this in truth, gold-coloured one."
[Shri said:] "I am beloved of the world; good fortune to you. I am famed here by the name Shri. The Daityas, abandoned by me, were destroyed for everlasting years.
Indra, Vivasvan, Soma, Vishnu, water and fire, those whom I approach, prosper, and so sages and gods.
Those whom I hate, cows, perish entirely, and lacking dharma, wealth and desire, are joined with unhappiness.
Know me, cows, to be of such power, a giver of happiness; I wish to live in all of you always; I have come asking, honoured by you, sinless ones."
[Shri said:] "What is this, cows, that you do not welcome me here? Why do you not accept me, hard to get and good?
This popular saying goes about the world, good ones, and is true: when one comes of oneself, disrespect results; that is certain.
Men serve me after fierce great austerity, and gods, danavas, gandharvas, pishachas, serpents and rakshasas.
It is fit for you, cows, to accept me here; I am not to be slighted, gentle ones, in the three worlds with moving and unmoving."
[The cows said:] "We do not slight you, goddess; we do not scorn you; you are unsteady and fickle-minded, therefore we avoid you.
What is the use of saying much here? Go where you wish; we are all well-formed; what is your use to us, sinless one?"
[Shri said:] "I shall be disregarded in all worlds, givers of honour, by your refusal; show me favour.
You are greatly fortunate, refuges for those who take refuge; always protect me, faultless one, who serve you; I wish to be honoured by you, always auspicious ones.
I wish to live even in a single place of your bodies, even a most despised one; but there is nothing despised seen in your limbs, sinless ones.
Holy, pure, fortunate ones, give me an order; you ought to tell me in which limb I should dwell."
[Bhishma said:] Thus addressed, those fortunate cows, tender and kind, consulted together and said to Shri, king:
You must certainly be honoured by us, glorious one; live in our dung and urine; that is holy to us, fortunate one.
[Shri said:] "By good fortune this favour was done to me by you who show kindness; so be it, good fortune to you; I am honoured, givers of happiness."
[Bhishma said:] Having made this agreement with the cows, Shri vanished there as they looked on, Bharata.
This, son, I have told you of the greatness of cow dung; hear again as I speak of the greatness of cows.
Without curds and ghee here, sacrifice does not proceed; by them is the sacrificial nature of sacrifice, and thus the root is seen.
Of all gifts the gift of cows is praised; cows are best and pure, the highest purifier.
One should serve them for nourishment and also for peace; their milk, curds and ghee are release from all sins.
Cows are called supreme splendour here and hereafter; there is nothing more holy than cows, bull among men.
On this too they recite this ancient Itihasa, the conversation of the grandfather and Indra, Yudhishthira.
When the Daityas had been overcome and Shakra was lord of the three worlds, all creatures were joyful, devoted to truth and dharma.
Then sages with gandharvas, kinnaras, serpents and rakshasas, gods, asuras and suparnas, and lords of creatures attended the grandfather once, Kauravya.
Narada and Parvata, Vishvavasu, Haha and Huhu, singing divine melodies, attended that lord.
In that assembly of gods, a gathering of all beings, resounding with divine instruments and surrounded by divine women and Charanas, Indra, saluting and bowing, asked the lord of the gods:

Blessed one, grandfather, why is the world of cows above the gods who are lords of worlds? I wish to know this.
mahabharata:13:82.13	What austerity or celibacy was done here by cows, lord, that they live happily, free of dust, above the gods?
There Brahma said to Shakra, slayer of Bala: "Cows have always been disregarded by you, slayer of Bala.
Therefore you do not know their greatness; hear that, lord; the power and supreme greatness of cows, best of gods.
Cows are called a limb of sacrifice and sacrifice itself, Vasava; without them sacrifice does not go on in any way.
They support the creatures with milk and offerings, and their offspring take to ploughing.
They produce grain and various seeds; from these sacrifices proceed, offerings to gods and ancestors everywhere.
Milk, curds and ghee, and these holy ones, lord of gods, carry various burdens, oppressed by hunger.
They support the sages here and creatures by their work; by their work and good deeds they bear Vasava's peak; therefore they live above us always.
This is the reason, Shakra, for their dwelling today; the position of cows above the gods has been told, Shatakratu.
These are given boons and are boon-givers, Vasava, Saurabhis, of meritorious deeds, purifying, with auspicious marks.
And hear fully from me, slayer of Bala, why the Saurabhis went there, best of gods.
Long ago in the age of the gods, dear one, when great-souled lords of the Daityas ruled the three worlds and Vishnu had gone to the embryo,
Aditi was practising fierce austerity for a son, best of immortals, always on one foot.
Seeing that great goddess practising great austerity, Daksha's daughter, the goddess named Surabhi,
practised fierce austerity, glad and devoted to dharma, on the lovely peak of Kailasa, served by gods and gandharvas.
She stood on one foot, resorting to supreme yoga, for ten thousand years and a thousand years.
Tormented by her austerity, the gods with great sages and great serpents went there with me and attended that fortunate one.
Then I said to that goddess rich in austerity: "Why do you practise fierce austerity, goddess, blameless one?
I am pleased with you, greatly fortunate one, by this austerity, auspicious one; choose a boon, goddess; I shall give it, Purandara."
[Surabhi said:] "The boon is already done for me, blessed grandfather of the world; this is my boon today, that you are pleased with me, sinless one."
[Brahma said:] To that goddess Surabhi, lord of the gods, speaking so, I replied, hear that, lord of Shachi:

Because you wished without greed, goddess, and by your lovely austerity, I am pleased; therefore I give you the boon of immortality.
mahabharata:13:82.35	You will live above the three worlds, and by my grace the world of cows will be famed.
mahabharata:13:82.36	Your children, born of your deeds, will dwell among men making creatures, and all your daughters.
mahabharata:13:82.37	The enjoyments, divine and human, thought of by you in mind, and the happiness of heaven, goddess, will be yours, auspicious one.
Her worlds, thousand-eyed, are joined with all desires; there death does not enter, nor old age, nor fire; nor misery nor anything inauspicious is there, Vasava.
There are divine forests, divine houses and cars that go at will, Vasava, yoked.
By various holy vows, by serving sacred fords, by great austerity and by good deeds, the world of cows can be reached, lotus-eyed one.
All this has been told by me to you, Shakra, as you asked; you must not slight cows, slayer of foes.
[Bhishma said:] Hearing this, the thousand-eyed always honoured them and showed them great regard, Yudhishthira.
All this has been told to you, purifying, greatly radiant one; the supreme holy greatness of cows, the best, has been recited, tiger among men, destroying all sin.

One who, composed, always tells this to brahmanas, in offerings to gods and ancestors and at sacrifices and ancestral rites, gains an imperishable satisfaction of all desires that attends his ancestors.
A man devoted to cows gains whatever he desires; women devoted to cows would also gain their wishes.
One wishing a son gains a son, a maiden a husband, one wishing wealth gains wealth, one wishing dharma gains dharma.
One wishing learning gains learning, one wishing happiness gains happiness; nothing is hard to get for the devotee of cows, Bharata.

[Yudhishthira said:] Kingship is constant sorrow, and the stages are very hard to know; with a household there is sorrow, hard to bear for the unpractised; and for kings in general no good goal is found.
They are purified here constantly who give the earth; and the dharmas were told to me earlier by you, descendant of the Kurus.
Thus the gift of cows was told by you, Nriga; it was shown earlier by the sage Nachiketas.
In the Vedic Upanishad and in all rites, the fee in all sacrifices has been specified: land, cows and gold.
There the supreme Shruti says "Gold is the fee"; I wish to hear this truly, grandfather.
What is gold, how was it born, at what time and of what nature? What gift is it, what fruit, and why is it called supreme?
Why do the wise honour the gift of gold? And why is it praised as a fee in sacrificial acts?
Why is gold a better purifier than land and cows, and highest as a fee? Tell me, grandfather.
[Bhishma said:] My father, Shantanu of great splendour, had died; wishing to give him the funeral rite, I went to the gate of the Ganga.
Arriving there, son, I began the funeral rite for my father, and my mother Jahnavi helped me then.
Then, seating many sages perfected by austerity in front, I began the rites from the giving of water.
Having completed the earlier rite as prescribed, composed, I began rightly to give the offering as is right.
Then, breaking through that arrangement of kusha grass, a hand with a lovely armlet and hanging ornaments rose up, lord of men.
Seeing it rise, I came to supreme wonder: my father himself, as taker, bull of the Bharatas.
Then I had a thought again, considering the scripture: this rule is not laid down in the Vedas, "a hand"; the rice-ball is to be given by a man here; that was my mind.
The ancestors do not take in person here from a man, hidden somewhere; they take as prescribed; so the rice-ball should be given even on kusha grass.
Then I disregarded that showing of my father's hand, remembering the subtle rule by the authority of scripture, king.
Then I gave all that on the kusha grass, bull of the Bharatas, following the path of scripture; know that, best of men.
Then that hand of my father vanished, lord of men; then the ancestors showed themselves to me at the end of a dream.
Pleased, they said to me: "We are pleased, bull of the Bharatas, that by this knowledge you are not deluded in dharma.
By you acting by scripture, king, the standard here is the self, dharma, learning, the Vedas, ancestors and great sages,
the grandfather Brahma himself, the teachers and the Prajapati, brought forward as authority, and the order is not shaken.
This was well begun by you today, bull of the Bharatas; but let gold be given for land and cows.
Thus we and dharma and all our grandfathers will be purified, for that is the highest purifier.
Those who give gold carry across ten before and ten after": so my ancestors said.
Then I, astonished, king, woke, lord of men, and set my mind on the gift of gold, bull of the Bharatas.
Hear also this ancient Itihasa, king, of Jamadagni's son, lord, giving grain and long life.
Long ago Rama, Jamadagni's son, joined with fierce anger, made the earth free of kshatriyas twenty-one times.
Reaching its gate, lay down a corpse somewhere; the one who turns back on seeing it, king of the earth, is Samvarta.
But I am a son; the blessed one is father, king and my teacher; and a son abides by the command of his father by dharma.
Then those women, rising from their golden seats and making him sit, said nothing to the great soul and stood around waiting on him.
And what other kings were named there of blazing forms, for how long did they stay in heaven? Tell me that too.
